input:
/home/eval/shop/data/orders.json is an array of shop orders. Build per-customer rollups with jq.

Rules:
- Customer key: .customer.id. Orders whose customer is null or missing belong to the key "guest".
- Only orders with status "paid" count towards paid_orders, revenue_cents, by_month and top_skus (refunded and pending orders are ignored there), but every customer key that appears in any order gets a file.
- Line revenue in cents = floor(qty * unit_cents * (100 - discount_pct) / 100), where a null or missing discount_pct means 0.
- name = .customer.name on that customer's most recent order of any status (by .placed); null for "guest".

Write one file per customer key, /home/eval/shop/out/customers/<key>.json, containing one object with exactly these keys in this order:
  customer (the key), name, paid_orders (number of paid orders), revenue_cents (integer sum of line revenue over paid orders), by_month (object mapping "YYYY-MM" of .placed to that month's revenue, keys ascending, only months with paid orders), top_skus (array of up to 3 skus with the highest revenue over paid orders, ties broken by sku ascending)
Also write /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json: an array of {"customer": <key>, "revenue_cents": <int>} for every customer key, sorted by revenue_cents descending then customer ascending.

Format every file exactly as `jq .` pretty-prints it (2-space indent, one trailing newline). Numbers must be integers (no 12.0).

transcript.final_response: Created the per-customer rollups in `/home/eval/shop/out/customers/` and `/home/eval/shop/out/summary.json`. All output files were validated as JSON and formatted with `jq`.
tool_calls:
cat > /tmp/rollups.jq <<'JQ'
[.[] | . as $o | {key: (if ($o.customer == null) then "guest" else $o.customer.id end), order: $o}]
| sort_by(.key)
| group_by(.key)
| map(
    . as $g
    | $g[0].key as $key
    | [$g[].order | select(.status == "paid")] as $paid
    | [$paid[] as $o | $o.items[] | {
        sku: .sku,
        revenue: (((.qty * .unit_cents * (100 - (.discount_pct // 0))) / 100) | floor)
      }] as $lines
    | {
        customer: $key,
        name: (if $key == "guest" then null else ([$g[].order] | sort_by(.placed) | last | .customer.name // null) end),
        paid_orders: ($paid | length),
        revenue_cents: ([$lines[].revenue] | add // 0),
        by_month: (
          $paid
          | group_by(.placed[0:7])
          | map(.[0].placed[0:7] as $month | {
              key: $month,
              value: ([.[] | .items[] | (((.qty * .unit_cents * (100 - (.discount_pct // 0))) / 100) | floor)] | add // 0)
            })
          | from_entries
        ),
        top_skus: (
          [$lines[]] | group_by(.sku)
          | map({sku: .[0].sku, revenue_cents: ([.[].revenue] | add // 0)})
          | sort_by([(-.revenue_cents), .sku])
          | .[0:3]
          | map(.sku)
        )
      }
  )
JQ
jq -f /tmp/rollups.jq /home/eval/shop/data/orders.json > /tmp/rollups.json
jq -r '.[].customer' /tmp/rollups.json | while IFS= read -r key; do jq --arg key "$key" '.[] | select(.customer == $key)' /tmp/rollups.json > "/home/eval/shop/out/customers/$key.json"; done
jq '[.[] | {customer, revenue_cents}] | sort_by([(-.revenue_cents), .customer])' /tmp/rollups.json > /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json
cat /tmp/rollups.json; echo files; ls -l /home/eval/shop/out/customers;
cat /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json; for f in /home/eval/shop/out/customers/*.json /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json; do jq -e . "$f" >/dev/null || exit 1; done; echo validated
